text: Noel Fielding (/ˈnəʊəl/; born 21 May 1973) is an English comedian, artist, and actor. In 1998, he co-created the comedy troupe The Mighty Boosh with Julian Barratt, playing the character Vince Noir and several others. Other notable roles include Richmond in the IT Crowd, the lead role of Dick Turpin in The Completely Made-Up Adventures of Dick Turpin (2024), and he has been a co-presenter of The Great British Bake Off since 2017. Fielding began performing stand-up comedy after graduating from art school in 1995 and first met Barratt in 1997 when they both performed at a pub in north London. In 1998, they performed their first comedy show together at Oranje Boom Boom, which was "very raw, but... hilarious," followed by a gig at Hen and Chickens Theatre in Islington, London. They took The Mighty Boosh to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival in 1998, then returned in 1999 with Arctic Boosh and in 2000 with Autoboosh. In 2001, The Mighty Boosh became a six-part radio show on BBC London Live, later transferring to BBC Radio 4. In 2004, it became an 8-part television show on BBC Three, airing for three series until 2007—20 episodes in total—with the first series set in a zoo operated by Bob Fossil, the second in a flat, and the third in a secondhand shop in Dalston called Nabootique. The show generated a cult following and won awards, with its style described as surreal, escapist, and new wave comedy. Fielding said he did all the animations for the first three weeks of the TV show, but due to lack of sleep, Ivana Zorn, Nigel Coan's partner, took over most of the painting, with Fielding designing the main characters. Fielding and Barratt formed Secret Peter Productions with Nigel Coan, who also directed and co-wrote Noel Fielding's Luxury Comedy and helped animate series 1 and 2 of The Mighty Boosh. Dave Brown contributed graphics, and Julian Barratt composed all the music. The Mighty Boosh won the Shockwaves NME Best TV Award three times in 2007, 2008, and 2010. In 2006, they toured with The Mighty Boosh Live, and in 2008–2009, they toured again with The Mighty Boosh Live: Future Sailors Tour. Fielding and Barratt wrote two film scripts that did not reach production—one a "Rocky Horror Picture Show type thing" with Barratt as a man believing himself to be the last human, and another an Arctic adventure—due to their interest in the Arctic. Fielding appeared as a team captain on Never Mind the Buzzcocks from 2009 to 2015 and again since 2021, achieving the record for the highest team score, and appeared on The Big Fat Quiz of the Year thirteen times between 2006 and 2017, including three with Russell Brand, nine with Richard Ayoade, and once with Eddie Izzard. He also appeared in Catherine Tate's TV movie Laughing at the Noughties (2011), performed Kate Bush's "Wuthering Heights" dance routine for Let's Dance for Comic Relief (2011), and took part in Channel 4's Comedy Gala in 2010 and 2014. In 2011, he produced his first solo series for E4, titled Noel Fielding's Luxury Comedy, which aired in January 2012 and had a second series in 2014 titled Noel Fielding's Luxury Comedy 2: Tales From Painted Hawaii. He also appeared in music videos for Mint Royale ("Blue Song"), Razorlight ("In the Morning"), Robots in Disguise ("Girl", "The Tears", "Turn It Up"), and Kasabian ("Vlad the Impaler", "Re-Wired", "La Fée Verte"), with the "Vlad" role reprised at the 2014 Glastonbury Festival. Fielding was scheduled to appear in the 2007 film Stardust but dropped out due to ill health. In November 2007, he starred in five episodes of Vic Reeves' House Arrest as a local vagrant. He was born in the Westminster area of London in 1973, the son of Royal Mail manager Ray Fielding and Yvonne Fagan, and grew up in Mitcham, Southwest London. He is of French descent through his father, who Fielding described as "..basically French," and when he was three, his father remarried, and Fielding was mostly raised by his paternal grandmother. His father and stepmother, Diane, became more involved in parenting during his mother's illness in the 1980s, and his mother died in 1990 at age 37 from complications of liver damage. Fielding has commented that "My parents had lots of parties... They were hopelessly bohemian." Michael Fielding, his younger paternal half-brother, played various characters in The Mighty Boosh and Noel Fielding's Luxury Comedy, and his father and stepmother appeared in The Mighty Boosh, with his father making cameos as Chris de Burgh. When Fielding was around 6 or 7, he attended a Kiss concert, wearing a Kiss costume and was taken to the backstage dressing room so Gene Simmons could see it. At age 13, he began writing comedy sketches, and at 15, he became a goth and started using makeup, saying he loved being dressed up by his girlfriends. While studying at Croydon Art College, he met Dave Brown. From 1992 to 1995, he studied a BA in graphic design and advertising at Buckinghamshire College of Higher Education in High Wycombe, graduating in 1995. While at the college, Dave Brown and Nigel Coan were also on the same course, and all three shared a student house. Nigel Coan later collaborated with Fielding on The Mighty Boosh. After university, Fielding began performing comedy and started stand-up after graduating in 1995. In 1997, he first met Barratt at a pub in north London, where they both performed. Barratt had more experience in performing than Fielding, but they "had quite a good chemistry straight away." On the day they met, they went back to Barratt's place, where Barratt played music on his Akai sampler and Fielding used a ping-pong ball to make an eye patch. Both shared an interest in music—Fielding into rock and pop, Barratt into jazz and electro—and both had played in bands before meeting. They also shared a love of comedy, including Vic Reeves and Bob Mortimer. In 2010, Fielding was scheduled to perform a solo tour but cancelled it via Twitter, stating he was too busy to write the Mighty Boosh film and create a new album. In 2012, he toured Sydney and Melbourne with a solo stand-up show and hosted a stand-up comedy gala at the Just For Laughs festival in Sydney. From 2014 to 2015, he toured the UK and Australia with An Evening With Noel Fielding, which included stand-up, sketch comedy, and performances by his brother Michael Fielding and long-term collaborator Tom Meeten, with Nigel Coan creating the animation. In 2005 and 2010, Fielding performed at Montreal's Just For Laughs comedy festival, and in 2020, the festival moved online due to the COVID-19 pandemic, during which Fielding and Jimmy Carr live-streamed a conversation from their homes. Barratt and Fielding first performed together in Stewart Lee's show Moby Dick and King Dong (Edinburgh Fringe Festival, 1997), in which Barratt played King Dong's penis. The name "Mighty Boosh" originated from a phrase used by a friend of Michael Fielding's to describe Michael's childhood hair. Fielding and Barratt said they used to place potted plants around Hen and Chickens to try and make it into a play, though they "didn't know anything about theatre or what you did." Fielding has said that his show is "magical and fantastical," telling intricate, weird stories, with Vince Noir being a modern, indie kid and Howard Moon being eccentric, relying heavily on Barratt's music and his own animation. Fielding formed Secret Peter Productions with Nigel Coan, and Coan also directed and co-wrote Noel Fielding's Luxury Comedy. In 2017, it was revealed that Fielding would co-host The Great British Bake Off with Sandi Toksvig. In 2017, he appeared as a contestant on Taskmaster (Series 4), hosted by Greg Davies and Alex Horne, and won the series. In January 2018, he was a panellist on QI alongside Russell Brand and Aisling Bea. In 2024, he played Dick Turpin in The Completely Made-Up Adventures of Dick Turpin on Apple TV+. Fielding has exhibited his artwork in London and collaborated with Fendi for their autumn/winter 2021 menswear collection.

Noel Fielding made a brief appearance in the opening sequence of the film Baby Driver (2017) and appeared in the music video for Razorlight's "In the Morning". He featured in music videos for Robots in Disguise songs "Girl" (alongside Chris Corner, who was at the time boyfriend to Sue Denim), "The Tears", and "Turn It Up". In 2009, he was involved in the Kasabian video "Vlad the Impaler", in which he plays the titular character, and reprised the role at the 2014 Glastonbury Festival. The music video was directed by Richard Ayoade; Fielding is referenced in Kasabian's "La Fée Verte", a track on their Velociraptor! album, with Sergio Pizzorno noting "The line, 'I met Dalí in the street.' Dalí is Noel Fielding. And he is the modern-day Dalí". He also appears as Vlad in the "Re-Wired" video, riding a five-seater bicycle with the band, and as a patient in a psychiatric hospital in "You're In Love With a Psycho", re-enacting the broken mirror routine from the Marx Brothers film Duck Soup with Pizzorno and Tom Meighan. He appeared in Kate Bush's music video "Deeper Understanding" as a thank-you for the Let's Dance For Comic Relief performance. Fielding formed a band called Loose Tapestries with Sergio Pizzorno to provide music for Noel Fielding's Luxury Comedy; the band released two albums and a Christmas single. Fielding has exhibited his paintings in London; his first exhibition, entitled Psychedelic Dreams of the Jelly Fox, took place in December 2007 in a gallery above the patisserie Maison Bertaux in Greek Street, Soho. There, he listed inspirations including Henri Rousseau, René Magritte, Willem de Kooning, Roy Lichtenstein, Dexter Dalwood, a former tutor from the Croydon School of Art, and Salvador Dalí. A second exhibition, Bryan Ferry vs the Jelly Fox, ran from 5 July 2010 to 5 January 2011 at Maison Bertaux. In October 2011, he released an art book titled Scribblings of a Madcap Shambleton, co-produced with The Mighty Boosh cast member Dave Brown, featuring many of his old and new paintings, drawings, and photography. His video installation of The Jelly Fox was shown at the Saatchi Gallery, and in 2012 he created a unique piece inspired by The Beatles for Liverpool Love at the Museum of Liverpool. In March 2015, his exhibition He Wore Dreams Around Unkind Faces was shown at the Royal Albert Hall. In January 2021, luxury fashion house Fendi unveiled a collection featuring abstract takes on the brand's logo, created by Fielding. On 18 November 2025, British rock band Pink Floyd released a newly mixed version of Shine On You Crazy Diamond (Parts I–IX) along with an official YouTube video featuring a time-lapse painting by Fielding inspired by founding member Syd Barrett. On 6 September 2011, Fielding received an honorary master's degree from his alma mater, now called Buckinghamshire New University, for his ongoing interest in the graphics area and support for many art organisations. In 2015, Fielding was named one of GQ magazine's 50 best-dressed British men. He was formerly in a relationship with Robots in Disguise lead vocalist Dee Plume, who made minor appearances in The Mighty Boosh and its live adaptations. He began dating radio DJ Lliana Bird around 2010, and they have two children. During his time at art college, Fielding developed what was suspected to be the virus hepatitis A, though it was later confirmed to be glandular fever; Nigel Coan, who studied the same course at art college and shared a flat with him, helped Fielding during this period. Fielding was ill and exhausted for a year. His paternal half-brother is Michael Fielding.
